acceptance: Executable scenarios in Theseus and BenchBox prove that removing any single provider (each of anthropic, openai-codex, google-antigravity, and any future one) leaves the gateway startable, hosted and local reviews working on the remaining providers, and pr-open usable. Each substitution is reported on the PR.

When no remaining served model meets the PR's tier or capacity, the verdict and gate stay pending with an explicit `unavailable` cause. Nothing merges with a weaker review, and no attempts or retry budget are spent.
A develop config naming a dead provider is harmless: its removal PR gets a normal hosted review, with no ruleset relaxation.
A lost broker login or a provider outage is reported within one hour, through a host notification and a GitHub issue or a red CI health job.
No source file in either repository hard-codes a required provider list. A guard test enforces it.
Owner decisions in the plan's decision section are recorded before implementation.
context:
Owner decisions, 2026-11-06 (numbering per the plan's decision table):
- D1: a role's fallback chain is the list of qualified substitutes for every failure mode.
- D2: YES. google-antigravity/claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 go first in the anthropic opus and sonnet chains, after checking Antigravity quota and terms.
- D3: a deliberate removal is a notice, plus "develop still names p".
- D4: a red scheduled health job, plus a host-side issue through the owner's gh.
- D5: pr-open opens a draft with a marker when the local review is unavailable, for availability causes only.
- D6: classifier.unavailable_bucket = large. (The owner chose large over the recommended max; this accepts a risk of under-reviewing a huge change during a TypeSafe outage.)
- D7: owner interactive omp `fallbackOn: any`; the review config stays `usage-limit`. Applied to ~/.omp/agent/config.yml.
- D8: resilience ships as Theseus v0.2.2; the stdin/legacy cleanup is renumbered to v0.2.3.
- D9: at least 2 providers per role.
- D10: a substitute may answer follow-up rounds (the tier is the reviewer identity), with the model shown in the body.
- D11: CI detects by model listing, plus host `omp auth-gateway check` usage probes; no paid completion probes.
